editorial:
Imagine being a powerful king who thinks everyone loves him, only to find out he was totally wrong. You get to watch Lear make a huge mistake when he asks his daughters to brag about how much they love him just to get a piece of his land. Two of them lie through their teeth to get the money, while the one daughter who actually cares stays quiet. It feels like a giant family fight that goes way too far, and you can really feel the tension as the king realizes he gave everything to the wrong people.

What really hits home is the acting, which feels raw and real rather than like a stiff stage play. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you aren't into heavy drama. It is a great pick if you love stories about betrayal and family secrets. Since this is an older film, you should try to find the best version possible.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart in the end. After a big battle, Lear finally reunites with his favorite daughter, Cordelia. However, the tragedy does not stop there. Cordelia is killed while she is a prisoner, and Lear dies of a broken heart while holding her body. The evil daughters also meet bad ends, as they turn on each other and die. It is a sad finish where almost everyone loses everything.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about family betrayal.
